claims.head: Lankinen isn’t cursed against the Oilers
claims.body: Lankinen has been shaky against the Oilers since 2023-24, well below his usual. It looks like a pattern, but across three seasons a goalie’s record against one team told us nothing about the next meeting. Expect the usual Lankinen.
claims.nums: 6 starts against Edmonton: .855 save percentage · .894 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Lankinen’s record against the Oilers.
claims.call: If Lankinen starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .894 than to his .855 against the Oilers.
claims.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 6 against Edmonton, 3,059 shots against everyone else

check.rule: held if he starts and his save percentage is closer to his usual than to his record against this team; can't judge if he doesn't start

claims.head: Special teams lean toward the Oilers
claims.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.6 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Oilers’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Canucks’ kill is near the bottom of the league. The Canucks need to stay out of the box.
claims.nums: Edmonton 1st for power play (9.6 expected goals per 60) · Vancouver 27th for penalty kill
claims.gist: The Oilers’ power play has a soft target in the Canucks’ kill.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season

check.measure: expected goals per 60 on the power play
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Oilers should get some good looks
claims.call: The Oilers’ average shot has at least their usual 6.5% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Canucks have struggled to prevent dangerous shots, and the Oilers don’t waste many.
claims.nums: Edmonton 8th for shot quality (a 6.5% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Vancouver 31st for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: The Oilers make their shots count, and the Canucks allow dangerous ones.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season

check.measure: the average shot’s chance of going in, by expected goals
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Oilers’ defense joins the attack; the Canucks’ stays home
claims.body: On shots from defensemen, Edmonton is one of the league’s best and Vancouver is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
claims.gist: The Oilers and the Canucks sit at opposite ends for shots from defensemen.
claims.call: The Oilers’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Canucks’.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season

check.measure: share of 5-on-5 shot attempts taken by defensemen
check.rule: held if the team comes out ahead by at least half its usual margin; partly if it comes out ahead by less; otherwise didn't happen

VAN.head: A steep climb for Vancouver
VAN.body: Edmonton has controlled the play far better over recent games and Vancouver has home ice. Vancouver’s best hope is a power play that gets going, plus a big night in goal.

EDM.head: A big edge for Edmonton
EDM.body: Edmonton has controlled the play far better over recent games and Vancouver has home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Vancouver can make a game of it if their power play gets going.

story.head: McDavid’s favourite opponent
paras: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Oilers come in at 1-0-1, the Canucks at 1-1-0.
Don’t read much into Lankinen’s record against the Oilers. The Oilers’ power play has a soft target in the Canucks’ kill.
